name: OPTIS Product Options
summary: Shopify app that adds text boxes, swatches, file uploads and price add-ons to product pages, with conditional logic on paid plans and a free plan for 10 option sets.
best_for: Shopify stores that sell personalised or made-to-order products and need customers to enter text, upload files or pick extras before checkout
skip_if: you need a badge-free storefront on the free plan, or you want proof that price add-ons and file uploads work before you install
honest_knock: Price add-ons, conditional logic and import and export need a paid plan. The listing says the free plan has no watermark, but a Powered by OPTIS Product Options badge showed under our field on the free plan. The app editor showed in Dutch and ignored our request for English. The app edits what shoppers see through an app embed that you switch on in the theme.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Advanced · per month, Advanced, the first paid plan, as listed on the Shopify App Store on 22 November 2026
pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-22 on apps.shopify.com/product-options-by-bss) Free plan: 10 variant option sets, 10+ product option types, analytics, email and live support, watermark removed. Advanced is $9.99 a month: unlimited option sets, 15+ option types, price add-on, conditional logic, import and export, 5 file uploads per button and option styling, with a 14 day free trial. Platinum is $19.99 a month: unlimited option types and features, 20 file uploads, option quantity, calendar language, editing options on the cart page and prioritised support, with a 14 day trial. Unlimited is $49.99 a month, for Shopify Plus: customisation service and 1-1 support, with a 14 day trial. All charges are billed in USD every 30 days. On our development store Shopify showed the Advanced Plan as a test charge of $9.99 every 30 days and we paid nothing.

compare_with.name: Shopify's own product variants
compare_with.why: Shopify variants limit how many options a product can carry and cannot take free text. OPTIS adds text boxes, file uploads, swatches and extra-priced options on the product page, with a free plan with 10 option sets, so you can try a custom text field on a store on any plan before paying.

sessions.what: Our AI assistant ran the test on 21 November 2026 on a Shopify development store with the Basic plan, in the real admin. We installed OPTIS Product Options from its Shopify App Store page, stayed on the free plan, saved one option set with an Engraving text field and opened the Advanced plan approval screen. The option was saved about 2.5 minutes after pressing Install and showed in the store preview about 3 minutes after install, once we switched on the app embed. Shopify marked the plan as a test charge that is not billed, so we paid nothing.
findings: Install: the Shopify dialog asked for view access to customer data, device and activity data, and staff and contributor data, and to view and edit customers, products, orders, discounts, Shopify Functions, the Online Store and custom data.

Option set: we created an option set with a text field labelled Engraving text on a snowboard. The preview of our store showed the field on the product page after we switched on the app embed and saved the theme change.

Badge: the field showed a "Powered by OPTIS Product Options" line under it while we were on the free plan. The Shopify App Store listing lists "Watermark removed" under the free plan, so the listing and what we saw differ; we did not find out why.

Plan: the approval screen showed the Advanced Plan at $9.99 every 30 days with a 14 day free trial ending on 5 December, and the line "You will not be billed for this test charge". We cancelled the screen and stayed on the free plan.
Language: the app editor showed in Dutch because of our browser language, and adding ?locale=en did not change it. The store preview was in English. The listing says the app supports 22 languages.
not_tested: Not tested: price add-ons, variant options, file uploads, other option types, conditional logic and a real order with an option.
Not tested: paying. Shopify showed a test charge on our development store, so we cannot say how the trial converts or what a real invoice looks like.
Not tested: uninstalling. The app stayed on our development store on the free plan.
